_comment: Issue #587 C1 initial budgets, completed in #656 Layer 1F. EVERY rig under tests/perf and tests/scale must be registered here — scripts/test-report/validate-nightly-wiring.mjs fails when a rig file has no entry (or an entry names a rig that no longer exists), so a new rig cannot land unbudgeted and a deleted one cannot rot here. Each rig records wall-clock nightly; after `minimumSamples` observations it fails above `regressionMultiplier` x the trailing median. `budgetMs` is the optional ABSOLUTE catastrophic-failure ceiling a rig enforces before that distribution exists; it lives here rather than as a constant inside the rig so `bun run test:ratchet` can hold it tighten-only (this file is a PERF_BUDGET_SOURCE). A rig with no `budgetMs` either carries per-measurement budgets in its own body or has no absolute ceiling by design — no absolute latency budget is invented before the distribution exists.
_drift: Issue #659 R4. `minimumSamples`/`regressionMultiplier` describe the LEGACY catastrophe gate in @centraid/test-kit's qualityRegressionBudget (10 samples, 3x median) — a 3x median only fires on a collapse, and until #659 the rigs with a fixed absolute ceiling did not consume history at ALL, so a rig could drift from 40 ms to 110 ms under a 120 ms ceiling with nothing to say. `minimumDriftSamples`/`driftMultiplier` are the sustained-drift gate every rig now also consumes via rigDriftBudgetMs() in tests/helpers/rig-budgets.ts: once 30 durable nightly observations exist, a measurement above 1.5x the trailing median fails. 30 samples ≈ a month of nightlies, which is long enough that a single slow runner cannot move the median and short enough that a real regression is caught in a release cycle. Both multipliers are CEILINGS under the tighten-only ratchet; both sample counts are min* FLOORS and may only rise.

tests/perf/blob-egress.perf.test.ts.volume: 128 MiB local blob egress — first byte + RSS in a forked child

tests/perf/desktop-cold.perf.test.ts.volume: 1 cold import of the desktop MAIN-PROCESS graph in a fresh child process with `electron` stubbed — apps/desktop/dist/main/local-gateway.js and the sibling main modules it drags in (430-431 modules since #883 C5, down from 1,001-1,003 in C1). Before #883 C1 this rig imported gateway-supervisor-core.ts, a ZERO-import file, and timed one module parse.
tests/perf/desktop-cold.perf.test.ts._budgetMsNote: Ratcheted 3000 -> 1300 by #883 C5. C5 took the @centraid/server barrel off the main-process critical path (subpath imports in gateway-paths.ts/detached-gateway.ts, dynamic import of embedded-gateway.js) and 16 samples on a SHARED linux x64 container measured 396-431 ms at load average ~1.5 and 500-649 ms at load average ~8 (4 cores), against 952-1105 ms on the same host before the change. 1300 ms is ~3x the quiet-host maximum and ~2x the contended one, the same headroom convention the experience budgets use for a single-host measurement.

tests/perf/desktop-launch.perf.test.ts.volume: 1 REAL Electron cold launch (mock gateway, 1 app, fresh userData — an EMPTY vault, not year-3); measured by apps/desktop/tests/e2e/launch-time.spec.ts and consumed here as an artifact
tests/perf/desktop-launch.perf.test.ts._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. A cold Electron launch on a shared CI runner has no distribution yet; the gate is the 30-sample/1.5x drift budget. An absolute ceiling lands in tests/experience-budgets/desktop.json once ~10 green nightlies justify one.

tests/perf/gateway-request-volume.perf.t.volume: A YEAR-3-SHAPED vault seeded through packages/test-kit's seedYear3Vault — 5,000 core_party, 10,000 photos (one core_content_item + one media_asset each), 200 conversations x 12 turns, plus the sealed-locker and parked-action axes: ~27,600 domain rows and the replica change log their inserts produced. Then 30 serial GETs per core route (p95), one windowed replica bootstrap page lane, and one cold reopen of the SEEDED vault directory. A bounded approximation of the declared year-3 table (90,000 photo assets / ~22,000 turns) that a 60 s perf lane can build honestly (#883 C1)
tests/perf/gateway-request-volume.perf.t._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. The ceilings this rig asserts are `coreRouteP95Ms` and `gatewayColdStartMs` in tests/experience-budgets/gateway.json — the SAME entries the empty-vault forked-child lane (tests/perf/gateway-request.perf.test.ts) asserts, so the pair now fences both the transport floor and the volume case against one number. A separate absolute duration ceiling here would fence the seed, which is setup rather than measurement.

tests/scale/blob-gc.scale.test.ts.volume: 5,000 mixed-custody CAS objects on a real FS tier + 100,000 on an in-memory tier

tests/scale/large-vault.scale.test.ts.volume: 10,000 photos + 5,000 contacts + 1,000 notes, then daily-use queries

tests/scale/photos-timeline.scale.test.t.volume: 50,000 media assets spread over 3 years + a 10,000-photo one-calendar-day degenerate corpus, then their own ordered/bucketed reads

tests/scale/photos-memories.scale.test.t.volume: 50,000 media assets over a 3-year span (~27 trip blocks, ~1,500 capture-group/phash 'similar' pairs), then one rebuildMemories pass
tests/scale/photos-memories.scale.test.t._measured: Three consecutive 2026-08-07 development-host runs measured 1,153 ms / 14,921 ms / 2,399 ms (365 on-this-day, 28 trip, 1,000 similar memories, 58,394 member rows every run) — a shared, loaded dev host, not a clean bench. budgetMs is set as a catastrophic-failure ceiling well above the observed spread rather than tight headroom over the lowest sample; the 30-sample/1.5x drift gate (once it has history) is what actually tracks steady-state cost.

tests/scale/phash-clustering.scale.test..volume: 90,000 photo assets, 3,000 near-duplicate families — cold sweep + idle sweep

tests/scale/multi-vault-footprint.scale..volume: 5 mounted vaults = 10 SQLite handles (year-3 household: Personal auto-founded per #603, plus one shared or personal vault per additional member) under ONE host footprint budget
tests/scale/multi-vault-footprint.scale.._noBudgetMs: Not a duration rig. The ceilings are the host footprint totals themselves, read from DEFAULT_VAULT_FOOTPRINT, and the drift series is summed page cache in bytes rather than wall clock.

tests/scale/ontology.scale.test.ts.volume: 10,000 entities paged through Atlas kinds + relations

tests/scale/backup-manifest-size.scale.t.volume: manifests at 25k / 50k / 100k chunk-index entries — size growth bound

tests/scale/composite-load.scale.test.ts.volume: 20 ops on each of five HTTP lanes (windowed replica bootstrap, Notes search, Notes create-note, 64 KiB blob staging, Atlas ref-search) at 2 in flight, run once one-lane-at-a-time and once all together, plus 128 harness turn dispatches and a 200-automation missed-window scan during the together phase — one real serve() gateway, empty vault, eight bundled apps
tests/scale/composite-load.scale.test.ts._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. The ceilings are a RATIO and an absolute worst-lane p95, not a rig duration: `compositeLoadFactor` in tests/experience-budgets/gateway.json (ceilingThroughputFactor 2, ceilingWorstLaneP95Ms 3500), both asserted in the rig body and both tighten-only there. Total wall clock was 4.3-10.2 s across five 2026-08-21 runs on a contended 4-vCPU container — a 2.4x spread that is host contention, so an absolute duration ceiling here would fence the runner, not the product. The 30-sample/1.5x drift gate is the duration gate.

tests/scale/stress-to-failure.scale.test.volume: concurrency ladder 1/2/4/8/16/32/64/128 against the app-handler plane (255 requests) plus a 64-wide concurrent create-note write storm, then one recovery request and isolated integrity_check / foreign_key_check on the vault
tests/scale/stress-to-failure.scale.test._noBudgetMs: Deliberate — this rig deliberately runs PAST the knee, so its wall clock is dominated by how long the admission queue holds refused work (WORKER_MAX_QUEUE_WAIT_MS is 10 s). What it gates is the SHAPE of the failure: typed refusals only, 429/503 only, no dropped connections, notes committed == 2xx responses exactly, integrity ok, and recovery inside stressRecovery.ceilingRecoveryMs (1000 ms) in tests/experience-budgets/gateway.json. Ladder duration is fenced by the 30-sample/1.5x drift gate.

tests/scale/long-run-soak.scale.test.ts.volume: one long-lived serve() gateway looped for CENTRAID_SOAK_MINUTES (default 0.75 on the nightly lane = 22-54 cycles / 330-810 ops; the weekly lane sets hours). Each cycle is 3 ops on each of five lanes; samples RSS/heap/external/arrayBuffers, open descriptors, total gateway SQLite bytes and per-cycle wall clock
tests/scale/long-run-soak.scale.test.ts._noBudgetMs: Deliberate — the rig's duration is an INPUT (CENTRAID_SOAK_MINUTES), so a wall-clock ceiling on it would be circular. The ceilings are the growth ceilings in `soakDegradation` (tests/experience-budgets/gateway.json) and the recorded drift series is the latency-creep FACTOR (last third / first third of post-warm-up cycles), not a duration.

tests/scale/restore-10gib.scale.test.ts.volume: YEAR-3: 10 GiB of CAS bytes (CENTRAID_SCALE_RESTORE_GIB, default 10) across 4 MiB objects + 5,000 core_party rows + one content row per object — backup, restore, then foreign_key_check and integrity_check timed in ISOLATION on the restored vault.db
tests/scale/restore-10gib.scale.test.ts._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. Restore duration at this size has never been observed on CI hardware; inventing an absolute ceiling would be the guess this rig exists to replace. Gated by the 30-sample/1.5x drift budget once a distribution exists. The rig SKIPS unless CENTRAID_SCALE_RESTORE_GIB is set, so it cannot slow the normal nightly scale job or the PR lane.

tests/scale/browser-replica-query.scale..volume: YEAR-3: 50,000 replica rows in one entity inside the shipping client query core (ReplicaSqliteStore over a node:sqlite driver — the same read path web and native run), then three reads: a full-entity materialisation, a filtered + sorted 200-row page, and an `in` over 1,000 ids (#883 C1 before-instrument, re-baselined by C3 once the grammar was compiled to SQL)
tests/scale/browser-replica-query.scale.._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. The rig's ceilings are PER READ, not per rig — FULL_READ_CEILING_MS / FILTERED_READ_CEILING_MS / IN_READ_CEILING_MS in its own body, each asserted there — because one rig duration would say nothing about which of the three reads regressed. #883 C3 pushed the read grammar into SQL and the seeded `in` DEBT MARKER is paid: 122,300 ms observed on 2026-08-28 became 64-70 ms, so the three ceilings were tightened from 20,000 / 10,000 / 400,000 to 4,000 / 1,500 / 1,500 and the whole rig now runs in about six seconds instead of two to three minutes. All three stay tighten-only, and the 30-sample/1.5x drift gate is the steady-state gate.

tests/scale/photo-similarity.scale.test..volume: YEAR-3: 90,000 media assets each with one 512-float `embed-image` embedding (184 MB of float32 vectors), 8 planted near-matches, then one 20-hit semantic search through EACH shipping ranker (#883 C2, the measurement docs/decisions.md ruling Q12 defers the vector-engine choice to)
tests/scale/photo-similarity.scale.test.._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. The ceilings are PER ENGINE and per resource, not per rig — `photoSemanticSearchAtYear3` in tests/experience-budgets/gateway.json (ceilingMs, ceilingRssDeltaBytes, ceilingEventLoopBlockMs), each asserted in the rig body for both rankers — because one rig duration would be dominated by seeding 90,000 rows and would say nothing about which engine regressed. The 30-sample/1.5x drift gate is the duration gate.

tests/scale/replica-sse-fanout.scale.tes.volume: 16 concurrent replica SSE subscriptions against one real serve() gateway over a 2,000-row replicated table, then 50 commits pushed one at a time — each commit waited out to EVERY subscriber before the next is written (#883 C1's before-instrument, now C2's gate for the shared projection + subscriber cap)
tests/scale/replica-sse-fanout.scale.tes._measured: BEFORE (#883 C1): two 2026-08-28 runs on a shared 4-vCPU linux container measured 16,969 ms and 16,781 ms of fan-out wall clock (per-commit median 333/327 ms, p95 429/419 ms, 11,904/11,860 prepared vault statements PER COMMIT — about 744 per subscriber, the O(subscribers) projection cost this rig exists to witness); a third on the C2 container measured 13,443 ms at 10,784 statements. AFTER (#883 C2, routes/replica-fanout.ts — one commit registration and one memoised projection per (authorization x cursor) per commit generation, fanned to every subscriber): three consecutive runs on that same container measured 1,077 / 1,183 / 1,151 ms, per-commit median 19-21 ms, p95 53-54 ms, and 658 statements per commit on all three — one projection per commit rather than sixteen. budgetMs is ratcheted 45,000 -> 3,600, ~3x the worst of the three, the same contended-runner headroom convention the previous number used; the 30-sample/1.5x drift gate tracks steady state. The statement count is now ALSO gated, in the rig body (SHARED_PROJECTION_STATEMENTS_CEILING = 1,200), as a mechanism assertion rather than a cost budget — the rig's comment argues why that survives #873.

tests/scale/replica-reconnect.scale.test.volume: YEAR-3: 50,000 replica rows walked by a windowed HTTP bootstrap, a live change stream attached and then dropped, 25 commits written while the client is away, and the stale cursor resumed — reconnect-to-first-correct-frame (#883 C1, the probe tests/experience-budgets/gateway.json#reconnectToFresh asked for)
tests/scale/replica-reconnect.scale.test._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. The rig's own wall clock is dominated by seeding 50,000 rows and walking them through the bootstrap route — work that is SETUP for the measurement, not the measurement. What it gates is `reconnectToFresh.ceilingMs` in tests/experience-budgets/gateway.json (asserted in the rig body, tighten-only there), and the recorded drift series is the reconnect interval itself rather than the rig duration.

tests/scale/mobile-reconnect-to-fresh.sc.volume: YEAR-3: 50,000 mobile replica rows read through the native SQLite session, with 25 missed changes replayed after a background/foreground transition
tests/scale/mobile-reconnect-to-fresh.sc._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. The rig measures the client-side resume interval against `reconnectToFresh.ceilingMs` in tests/experience-budgets/mobile.json; setup and fixture construction are not the user-facing interval, and the 30-sample/1.5x drift gate tracks that interval once nightly history exists.

tests/scale/replica-bootstrap.scale.test.volume: 50,000 rows — client windowed bootstrap with an in-flight deletion, plus the gateway windowed-page walk resumed across a vault-plane restart (#750)

tests/scale/replica-retention.scale.test.volume: 45 simulated days x 4,000 replica writes (90% of them concentrated on 400 hot rows), run TWICE — once with the entry cap alone and once with compaction — then the worst-day resumable window measured on each (#883, the retention half of change-log.ts)
tests/scale/replica-retention.scale.test._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. What this rig gates is a WINDOW IN DAYS, not a duration: the worst day a returning phone can still resume from, asserted in the rig body against REPLICA_RETENTION_DAYS. The wall clock is dominated by seeding 360,000 writes twice, which is setup for that measurement rather than the measurement, and no absolute ceiling has a distribution behind it yet — the 30-sample/1.5x drift gate is the duration gate.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/cold-start..volume: 8 per-launch on-device cold starts against an EMPTY device replica (year-3 is 50,000 replica rows — see tests/experience-budgets/README.md)
tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/cold-start.._noBudgetMs: Deliberate. Simulator launch times have no distribution yet; the 30-sample/1.5x drift gate is the only gate until one exists.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/scroll-fram.volume: 8 flings each on the Photos grid and the People directory, holding whatever the CI gateway fixture seeded (year-3 is 90,000 photo assets / 5,000 contacts). The flow publishes `people rows observed` — a real lower bound it can see — rather than guessing the seeded total.
tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/scroll-fram._noBudgetMs: Not a duration rig. It measures dropped-frame PERCENT via apps/mobile's rAF sampler (arm with centraid://perf-frames, read testID perf-frame-report); the ceiling lives in tests/experience-budgets/mobile.json and the drift series is the worst dropped-frame percentage across the two surfaces. NOTE the denominator is per-device — targetHz is recorded beside every percentage — and the sampler sees the JS thread only.
